## Tensions

| # | Where | Note |
|---|-------|------|
| T-01 | [NIT-01.1](nightly/01-the-nightly-loop-and-run-state.md#nit-011-phases-of-a-night) | the at-most-once ordering is a documented caller contract on `persist` (`crates/dream-core/src/runstate.rs:615`); no code in this repository sequences it, so nothing here enforces it. Nothing records the forge push or the ledger commit either, so a crash after `Persisted` loses that night's publish and the restart finalises the night to `Complete` without reconciling against the forge; recovery is `reset_night` (`crates/dream-core/src/runstate.rs:401`). |
| T-02 | [NIT-02.2](nightly/02-replay-capture-and-verify.md#nit-022-what-verify-re-checks) | replay is not tamper evidence. Only the report and the config are digest-bound, so editing a receipt's exit status, outcome and streams together with `decision.json` defeats `verify` (`crates/dream-core/src/replay.rs:10`). A witness over the run directory is the stated remedy and lives elsewhere (`crates/dream-core/src/replay.rs:18`). |
| T-03 | [NIT-03.2](nightly/03-automerge-policy-decision-tree.md#nit-032-gathering-the-facts-in-publish) | the forge step is untested against live GitHub. The only test touching `GhForge` is a dyn-safety check (`crates/dream-core/src/seams.rs:647`), so the protection parsing, the draft-to-ready transition and the squash request have only been exercised against fakes. |
| T-04 | [GAT-01.5](gate/01-verdict-classes-and-the-decide-flow.md#gat-015-guard-resource-bounds-and-evaluator-command-paths) | command substitution is refused wherever it is not in single quotes, so a legitimate evaluator such as `cargo test $(nproc)` stops the night as `UnsupportedCommand` (`crates/dream-gate/src/guard.rs:557`); the rule is safe and blunt, and the evaluator has to be rewritten. |
| T-05 | [SEL-01.3](selection/01-pairwise-policies-and-the-fault-mapping.md#sel-013-from-per-test-results-to-vetoes) | only `Reject` is acted on (`crates/dream-gate/src/pertest.rs:304`). A policy that comes back `Inconclusive` on per-test evidence, for example because too many pairings faulted at the crate level, adds no veto here. Faults are caught separately by the harness veto at step 1, but the two layers are not obviously equivalent. |
| T-06 | [SEL-02.1](selection/02-failure-fingerprint-lifecycle.md#sel-021-from-text-to-identity) | the identity is 64 bits (`crates/failure-fingerprint/src/lib.rs:263`). Accidental digest collision risk grows with the number of identities. Encoding aliases and normalisation merges are separate risks that do not require a random digest collision. A match against a baseline failure suppresses this particular new-fingerprint veto; other gate checks can still reject the candidate. ADR-DE-004 lists a collision seen in practice as its review trigger. |
